items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One I knew before was Roger Paraboschi... and Benny Wasseur, trombone. The style of the band was a mixture of New Orleans and swing.

ctx.x: The corners of Boulevard St. Germain des Prés and rue de Rennes, St. Benoit and St. Germain were the most popular corners of the district, and had very large cafés, where the students,artists and friends met.

My favorite café was the Café St. Germain des Prés, and I eventually made many friends there, amongst them quite a number of African students and dancers. After a few days with Bolling, I became acquainted with the name of the musicians. One I knew before was Roger Paraboschi, the ex drummer of the Edouard's band. Jaques Hess played guitar, Maxime Saury, clarinet, Gille Thibault, cornet, Guy de Fatto, bass, and Benny Wasseur, trombone. The style of the band was a mixture of New Orleans and swing. I had heard that…

The Vieux Colombier was jumping and the young dancers had picked up long before I came to Paris on how to dance the jitterbug. The African students were the best dancers, but there were some French cats that were on the ball and gave the Africans a tight race. I don't have any idea of how long Bolling had been working at the Vieux Colombier, but his band and I finished there the 2nd of September.
